name_en: Kuey teow kerang (char kuey teow with cockles)
intro: A plate of kuey teow kerang is about 700 kcal (estimate). Most of the calories come from the kuey teow and the oil used when frying over high heat.
diet: Yes, but this is one of the highest-calorie fried noodle dishes. The cockles give some protein, but the oil and dark soy sauce push the calories up. Treat it as something to enjoy once in a while, not an everyday meal. If you had it for lunch, go for a light, veggie-heavy dinner.
tips: Share a plate with your partner and add a plate of stir-fried vegetables or soup.
Ask for extra cockles and taugeh, less oil.
Skip extra fried food and sweet drinks. Go for plain water or limau ais kosong.

swap.name: Kuey teow kerang soup
swap.why: Almost the same ingredients with cockles and taugeh, but without all the frying oil.

faq.q: Are the half-cooked cockles in kuey teow safe to eat?
faq.a: Cockles are usually added at the end and cooked briefly. If you're worried, ask the hawker to cook them longer.

faq.q: Why does kuey teow kerang have that 'wok hei' taste?
faq.a: That smoky aroma comes from the high flame and very hot wok, with the soy sauce caramelising slightly during fast frying.
Cockles have cholesterol but are also high in iron and protein. Normal amounts are okay for most people. If you have health issues, check with your doctor.
